children.topic: The friend who took three pills
children.note:
A devotee in chronic pain was told to take one tablet, took three to kill the pain faster and nearly left his body. The doctor called him foolish — that is our situation. — “We are foolish.”

🎙 Maharaj at 50:12 (auto-transcript): “I have one good brother he told me that he told me that one time he was very sick and he was having a chronic pain it's not only him most of us have done the dissenting we have done dissenting many times so he was sharing his experience because we're having a good pain. So…”

If Krishna gave us all our reactions at once, we would die. So the physician spreads the dose through the day; we bear the pain we caused until the karma ends.

🎙 Maharaj at 51:34 (auto-transcript): “We are not just thinking of medicine. So if Krishna gives us everything that we need according to the magnitude of our simple activities, we will handle it, we will die. Therefore, Krishna's expert physician is giving us two pills in the morning, two in the afternoon, two in…”

Knowledge is not enough; applying it is character. Taking three pills when told one means thinking oneself superior to the doctor. A devotee stays fixed in practice without breaks, out of appreciation. — “application of the knowledge we get is important”

🎙 Maharaj at 52:27 (auto-transcript): “it should be clearly on the screen and applied application is very important not knowledge is important application of the knowledge we get is important therefore therefore character is power not knowledge application of the knowledge we have application that is character so…”

Complaints do not solve anything. Maharaj recalls a college prefect, a former military man, whose rule was that a punishment is obeyed first and argued afterwards. — “Obey before complaining.”

🎙 Maharaj at 54:14 (auto-transcript): “complaints will not help an issue Well, my college day, we have one prefect. Our prefect was a military man before he became a student in our college. His principle is obey before complaining. That was his principle. Obey before complaining. Even if you are right or wrong, he…”

The principle is accepted in ordinary life; we struggle with it in spiritual life because we are not grateful. Brahma is teaching us character.

🎙 Maharaj at 54:58 (auto-transcript): “so materially this principle is there why is it difficult for us in the spiritual sector because we are not grateful we are not grateful so here Obama is teaching us character the word indicate that a devotee endlessly awaits the mercy of the Supreme Lord, even while…”

Many say: I came to Krishna, chanted seriously, and my problems increased. Maharaj says Brahma has already answered this.

🎙 Maharaj at 56:28 (auto-transcript): “Yes, it's a question a lot of times. So that day we say, Christian, we're saying that the grammar has answered that question already. What was the question? We are trying seriously. We are told that, yeah, I come to Christian, your problem is finished. I came to Christian, I…”

Trouble that comes up when you sit to chant is the holy name throwing out what was stored in the heart. Let it go out; after a while it stops. — “it is working.”

🎙 Maharaj at 58:13 (auto-transcript): “You should understand that when you chance to sit down and you have so many problems, you should be intelligent to know that it is working. so it is breaking out all the dead which have been there so let it go out after some time you will see that you will no more experience…”

Sweeping a dirty room raises dust. Cover your nose and keep cleaning and soon the room is fit to sleep in; run out after a few minutes and the dust settles back in the room. — “you block your nose”

🎙 Maharaj at 59:02 (auto-transcript): “you know when you are cleaning a dirty room how do you feel you don't feel comfortable when you are cleaning a dirty room all the doors will rise so what to do mask you block your nose so you don't inhale it and keep cleaning if you do like that in a short while all the doors…”

children.topic: The body needs it — not you
children.note:
Someone argued that the body needs illicit sex. Maharaj replied that you are not the body; it is hard only because repetition has filled the mind with sweet memories that keep pulling. — “it's a body that needs it not you”

🎙 Maharaj at 61:41 (auto-transcript): “you know the doctor the body needs it yes the body needs it one day when when they told me he asked me a question i was explaining and i was saying there is no easy sex she said no the body needs it i said yes the body needs the body you are not the body you are not the body…”

A good doctor leaves no residue of disease. The purport explains that the hardship a sincere devotee meets is Krishna removing the last wish to enjoy — a cure from his own hand, not ordinary karma.

🎙 Maharaj at 63:56 (auto-transcript): “Christian wants to completely uproot the seed of sin as a good doctor. A good doctor should not treat depression and leave some residues from disease there. She will remove it completely. So Christian is diagnosing everything and giving the appropriate treatment. No remnant…”

After a free-writing reflection on trusting that Krishna knows what is best, Maharaj answers questions sent in and asked live.

🎙 Maharaj at 83:06 (auto-transcript): “Shilagurde, to start with, we have a couple of questions from yesterday's class. Yes. Yes, Shilagurde. The first question was from Paramakantin Mataji. Mataji was asking, she was expressing her gratitude. Thank you, Shilagurde, for the nectar. My question is, how to feel the…”

If Krishna is with us in his name, how can we ever feel intense separation from him?

🎙 Maharaj at 83:19 (auto-transcript): “The first question was from Paramakantin Mataji. Mataji was asking, she was expressing her gratitude. Thank you, Shilagurde, for the nectar. My question is, how to feel the intense separation from Krishna? When we have Krishna with us in the form of holy name will we ever…”

Separation must be practised, like an addict who craves even without the drug. Hearing the pastimes, a fortunate devotee laments that he was not there, and prays every day that it may become his experience too. — “if you don't practice it, you will not get it.”

🎙 Maharaj at 83:52 (auto-transcript): “Yes, the proper mention in this example that if you practice feeling suppression for the Krishna, if you practice it if you don't practice it, you will not get it. It's worth it because even if you are chanting the holy name, if you practice feeling suppression, you feel a…”

children.topic: Q2 · Are all of us in madhurya?
children.note:
Each soul has its own rasa, so how can everyone take part in the confidential pastimes of conjugal love?

🎙 Maharaj at 90:45 (auto-transcript): “not only madhurya rasa that that we have this not only Maduroans the cowhead boys they go to the forest they are friends not only Maduroans it is there it is there in any of the Rasa that we have a pleasure is there for us it is not it is not as much as we get in Maduro but…”

Pleasure is present in every rasa — the cowherd friends, the servants who cook, fetch water or make garlands. In the spiritual world nobody feels inferior or envious; scarcity belongs to this world.

🎙 Maharaj at 91:10 (auto-transcript): “in any of the Rasa that we have a pleasure is there for us it is not it is not as much as we get in Maduro but it is there therefore in the spiritual world nobody feels inferior other rassas therefore no one feels envious in a material sense the only enemy is there that we…”

When Krishna leaves a decision to us and no clarity comes, what should we do?

🎙 Maharaj at 96:01 (auto-transcript): “Maharaj, my question is that in a devotee's life everything is arranged by Krishna even it is good or bad it is for the devotee's good only but sometimes Krishna gives a little free will to choose and in that time I will be in the confusion to what to choose in my life and I…”

No speculation is needed: put the situation to your guru and he will direct you. That is how it has always been — the guru opens the eyes of one born in ignorance. — “You don't need to speculate.”

🎙 Maharaj at 96:31 (auto-transcript): “Ask your Christian master what to do. It will direct you. Not difficult. Ask you shall be. Ask you shall be. Given. So ask. What to do there? I say, this is my condition. What should I do in this case? We will tell you what to do. Simple. You don't need to speculate.”

How do we surrender fully to guru and Gauranga?

🎙 Maharaj at 98:13 (auto-transcript): “of businesses on to you guru maraj you said in the last that we should surrender to guru and goranga first is like what is surrender full surrender what is full surrender how to understand that and how we can surrender fully to guru and goranga so that means you should follow…”

Follow the instructions given and do nothing on your own. Do not ask the guru something and then decline the answer — that is not surrender, and it becomes an offence. — “Surrender means you don't have your independence.”

🎙 Maharaj at 98:29 (auto-transcript): “that and how we can surrender fully to guru and goranga so that means you should follow the instructions we've been giving to you. Don't do things on your own. Don't ask. When you depend on somebody, what you tell you to do and you're ready to do that. Don't go to the…”

children.topic: Q5 · How do pure devotees tolerate?
children.note:
Two questions: what lets pure devotees like the gopis tolerate so much, and isn't tolerance built simply by tolerating?

🎙 Maharaj at 100:22 (auto-transcript): “I have a question. so in today's session we were hearing that how great the quality of tolerance is for a sadhaka and how they should develop this because we have to look for krishna's mercy and how he's purifying us to bring us closer to him when we also see this quality in…”

Being pure, they see nothing wrong; they smile and accept it as Krishna's kindness. Absorbed within, they do not even hear the mockers — like Gaura Kisora, who heard neither praise nor blame.

🎙 Maharaj at 101:47 (auto-transcript): “They say pure, it means what? Pure, they are pure. Therefore, they don't see anything wrong. They see everything and Christian is missing. Christian is so kind to me, so he's giving me a little little talking. The reactions to myself, that's how they see it. Therefore, they…”

Keeping quiet while angry inside only means we cannot fight back; one day it explodes, and the hidden anger hurts people anyway. Real tolerance is a spiritual quality — being comfortable, without grudge, because one is pure. — “Tolerance is a spiritual quality.”

🎙 Maharaj at 108:13 (auto-transcript): “if you say something I'm keeping quiet means what I'm angry with you I'm angry that is not tolerant because I cannot fight you so I'm keeping quiet I'm feeling angry inside me I'm planning something against you don't worry if I see somebody angry with you I'll join the place…”

nodeData.topic: Day 07 · Repentance Without Bargaining
nodeData.note: SB 10.14.9-10 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Brahma feels ashamed of testing Krishna, and Maharaj shows why repentance is a sign of good fortune: a mistake is not the problem, repeating it is. Correction is love, as with children and with Indra. Brahma asks to be treated as a foolish dependent and, above all, not to lose his service; in the questions Maharaj speaks on inner chastisement, obtaining the forgiveness of those we offend, and saying sorry from the heart. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Brahma admits he tried to measure Krishna with his own power of illusion and now sees himself as a tiny spark before a blaze. Maharaj: Brahma is ashamed and repents.

Repentance is a mark of good fortune. Not everyone feels ashamed of something foolish or abominable. — “Repentance is very important.”

🎙 Maharaj at 44:18 (auto-transcript): “Repentance is very important. Repentance. The final of repentance is part of equity.”

One who sins proudly can never feel shame and so can never repent. Brahma is the opposite: he feels the shame of what he did.

🎙 Maharaj at 45:20 (auto-transcript): “The generation of sin with pride. Men are called sin with pride. So a person who is sinning with pride can never feel ashamed of this, therefore cannot repent. So Brahma is ashamed of what he did. He was unsivilized. In the beginning, he was thinking he was unsivilized to the…”

At first Brahma saw Krishna as an uneducated, uncivilised village boy — sitting with cowherd friends in the forest, holding his lunch, living among animals, without even shoes.

🎙 Maharaj at 45:57 (auto-transcript): “He was unsivilized. In the beginning, he was thinking he was unsivilized to the person. Krishna is the old boy, unsivilized, one educated. He is holding prasadam in the death of some culture. We were thinking about that. So, this unsivilized boy, he gave this to me. This boy,…”

The boys eat from one another's plates and feed Krishna; to Brahma this looked like children who know no manners. He could not understand what he was seeing.

🎙 Maharaj at 47:16 (auto-transcript): “They were eating food from their plate, telling Krishna, preparation is not in their plate. The Buddha doesn't know how to pose. The Buddha sees boys. They don't know how to be. They are associating with animals so they'll bring his life.”

A great fire throws out many sparks, but a spark cannot burn the fire it came from. Even the creator of the universe is a tiny potency next to Krishna, so Brahma's attempt was bound to fail.

🎙 Maharaj at 52:09 (auto-transcript): “So, painted from it. A great fire produces many sparks. A spark cannot produce. Depends on, if a spark falls in water, we produce another water, another fire. Before the sun, we produce. And Lord Krishna can light.”

Brahma now calls Krishna Isa, the master. Citing Jiva Gosvami, Maharaj notes that the word fits only the one who controls everything at all times — not Brahma, who has just been overcome by his own illusion.

🎙 Maharaj at 54:31 (auto-transcript): “addressing Lord Krishna as is, which indicates that Krishna is not only the Supreme Master of everyone, but is also specifically the Master of Brahma, who created the universe directly under the guidance of the Lord, and who indeed is born directly from the Lord. Obama did…”

Brahma only addressed Krishna this way after his mistake. Making a mistake is not the bad part; failing to learn from it is. Follow Brahma: learn and take the next step. — “To commit a mistake is not bad.”

🎙 Maharaj at 54:55 (auto-transcript): “Obama did not say that in the beginning, until he committed a mistake. To commit a mistake is not bad. I don't think a mistake is not bad. What is bad is that one learns from the mistake. If you follow Obama's footsteps, he learns from the mistake. Obama did not take enough…”

Repeating the same thing again and again is no longer a mistake but a choice. Doing it once and learning is progress in Krishna consciousness; repeating it means we are not growing. — “It is deliberate, not a mistake.”

🎙 Maharaj at 55:52 (auto-transcript): “We don't play for friends and repeat the same thing and repeat the same thing and repeat the same thing. It is not more a mistake, it is deliberate. It is deliberate, not a mistake. A mistake is one. We learn from it and from the next step. That is progress in Krishna…”

Brahma is willing to accept his master's punishment because he knows it corrects. Most of us lie to avoid punishment; Krishna disciplines his devotees so that their foolishness does not swallow their devotion.

🎙 Maharaj at 58:20 (auto-transcript): “He was therefore perfectly willing to be according to his disciples, punishment. We don't want to be punished, everyone will tell lies. You don't understand what you're saying. Your Brahma is ready to live on punishment because you know that punishment is for correction,”

children.topic: The child who is never corrected
children.note:
Parents who shield a child from every correction leave him helpless. When they are no longer there, who will protect him? Real protection includes training. — “What will the child do when they do not have a proper training”

🎙 Maharaj at 59:34 (auto-transcript): “It's a big lesson from all of us because when we think I'm protecting my, therefore if something wrong should not be, I'm a person superior, therefore my children should not be, my child should be. If you go like that, the child is not going to be a good child tomorrow, when…”

When Indra came to beg pardon, Krishna told him to go back to his post: he had not wanted Indra's position, he punished him because Indra is a devotee and should be a good one. — “I am not interested in your position.”

🎙 Maharaj at 60:54 (auto-transcript): “Krishna chastised a Lord, Indra. When Lord Indra came to obey Krishna, Krishna told him, go back to your own secret position. I am not interested in your position. I punish you because you are a devotee and I want you to be a good one. So you are thinking that I am taking…”

Responsible devotees keep seeing their own mistakes and begging forgiveness. Maharaj again recalls an acarya's saying that an advanced devotee prefers criticism to glorification.

🎙 Maharaj at 62:34 (auto-transcript): “The motives who are happy bring church. He mentioned one of our greater church. He said, He prefers criticism than glorifying. Don't glorify it. So, when we are criticizing the glorifying meeting, getting, we are thinking we are doing it. People doing that, we are putting…”
Brahma confesses that pride in being a controller blinded him, and appeals to Krishna to see him as a dependent servant and show compassion.

Through Visvanatha Cakravarti's commentary: Brahma pleads that he acted out of ignorance, like a foolish child. This is not flattery to escape — he leaves punishment or mercy to Krishna, because either one purifies. — “He wants to be punished.”

🎙 Maharaj at 65:54 (auto-transcript): “I did it that of ignorance. I don't know you. So, it is in a foolishness. Think of me, in a sense, a fool. He is not breaking the education to not punish him. He gave me punishment, petition, mercy. By this, I've got purified. He didn't say, I'm not sure in this, you don't…”

Brahma's real plea: punish me, but do not remove me from your service, because service is my link with you. — “that is my chance to be connected with you”

🎙 Maharaj at 68:16 (auto-transcript): “Don't sack me from my punishment, but don't sack me from me. Don't take my service away, because that is my chance to be connected with you in this. The opposite is, show me mercy by not giving me any service. Learn to be free, so I can do more safety, I can bring you more…”

We often pray the reverse: release me from service so I can be free — and then end up taking service from the guru instead of giving it. Then who is the master and who the servant?

🎙 Maharaj at 68:42 (auto-transcript): “The opposite is, show me mercy by not giving me any service. Learn to be free, so I can do more safety, I can bring you more services. What is our commercial world to use? What is our commercial world to use?”

Nothing in this world can satisfy the senses. Maharaj alludes to King Yayati, who even took his son's youth and still found no end to desire — a matter of shame.

🎙 Maharaj at 70:20 (auto-transcript): “When you come to satisfy your senses, the people will try to satisfy your senses. Brahma is succeeded. There will be anyone who will satisfy your senses in this world. Anyone? What do you think? Because of the power of Yahya, Yahya, Yahya, Yahya. Does anyone think? Does…”

children.topic: Position, not service, makes us proud
children.note:
Brahma's exalted post as creator tempted him to forget he is a servant. Service never makes anyone proud; position does. — “The service will not make one proud.”

🎙 Maharaj at 75:04 (auto-transcript): “His prestigious position as a cosmic creator also tends to identify himself as a lord of this world. And thus, he sometimes forgets his position as a servant of his power, as what position do. The service will not make one proud.”

After a free-writing reflection on confessing without bargaining, devotees ask live and in the chat.

🎙 Maharaj at 90:16 (auto-transcript): “moving on to the question and answer section so if devotees have any questions they may either raise their hands on zoom or type their question out in the chat box”

children.topic: Q1 · How do we know real chastisement?
children.note:
How can we tell whether what we suffer is the real correction the guru wants to give us?

A good devotee feels chastisement even when it is not spoken directly; inner, mental correction for a wrong act hurts more than physical punishment, and Maharaj calls it mercy.

🎙 Maharaj at 92:55 (auto-transcript): “If it goes to no, that chastisement is, even if it is not directly done to you, you will see, if you are a good devotee, you will see the earth, you will get it when the mental chastisement is worse than the physical material of you.”

children.topic: Q2 · I feel guilty, then repeat it
children.note:
Brahma and Madhai kept repenting after their offences; I feel guilt, forget, and do the same again. What to do?

🎙 Maharaj at 94:09 (auto-transcript): “i wanted to ask um i'm i'm seeing lord brahma”

Feeling bad is only the beginning. The key is to obtain the mercy of the person we offended; otherwise we repeat it. Madhai begged Nityananda Prabhu, and Brahma begged Krishna, who forgave him.

🎙 Maharaj at 95:53 (auto-transcript): “i do here when we when we wait for something wrong it is just the beginning that is just the beginning the most important part is to obtain the mercy of the person if we don't do that we'll commit again and again and again because there is no mercy to give all the strength of…”

children.topic: Q3 · The mood to accept correction?
children.note:
Should we wait for the guru to chastise us, and what mood lets us accept it as love?

🎙 Maharaj at 100:10 (auto-transcript): “So Maharaj, my question is if we follow the instruction of the spiritual master chant nicely and do everything nicely you become purified at the same time like when we do something wrong and the Guru chastises you it also purifies you so Maran my question is do we…”

Be ready to accept it as meant for you; that readiness comes from hearing, thinking and learning every day. — “So we should hear, every day.”

🎙 Maharaj at 101:39 (auto-transcript): “So, we should hear what is justice, we should hear. If you don't hear, then listen. So it is compulsory for us to hear, think and learn, to give a chance to hear. So we should hear, every day. That's what we should do.”

children.topic: Q4 · Why don't I see wrongdoing?
children.note:
Misdeeds happen in front of me and I only recognise them too late. Why?

🎙 Maharaj at 105:14 (auto-transcript): “So, Prabhuji is asking, Hare Krishna, dear Shla Gurudev, sometimes there are certain misdeeds or wrong activities that are happening right in front of me but we are not able to identify it or we are not able to recognize it what is the reason behind it and most of the times…”

nodeData.topic: Day 08 · What Am I Before You?
nodeData.note: SB 10.14.11 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Brahma measures himself against Krishna and finds there is no comparison, and Maharaj makes the point vivid: counting the souls in one tiny universe, asking who can walk out of it, and telling the Purana story of Narada searching for the greatest thing. Scripture puts us in our place so that we stay humble and paint our hearts with Krishna. In the questions he speaks on overcoming pride, making every day a festival, and seeing the cause rather than the instrument. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Brahma sets his small body and his universe of material elements beside Krishna, through whose body countless universes drift like specks of dust. Maharaj reads two translations and sums it up: there is nothing to compare.

children.topic: A torch pointed at the sun
children.note:

nodeData.topic: Day 09 · A Child Kicking in the Womb
nodeData.note: SB 10.14.12 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Brahma asks Krishna to treat his offence as a mother treats the kicks of the child in her womb, and Maharaj unfolds the image: our helplessness in the womb, Krishna's constant care, and Brahma's tactful plea that he is still a child within the Lord. Through the pastime of baby Nimai eating a brahmana's offering, he shows how a child's faults are met with laughter and how real practice shows in one's life. No questions were taken because of a network failure in Lagos. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Brahma calls Krishna Adhoksaja and asks whether a mother is offended when the child inside her kicks — and whether anything at all lies outside the Lord. Maharaj: the answer is no; everything is within him.

Some pregnant women complain of pain and blame everyone. But in truth a mother is happy to feel the baby move — and worried, off to the doctor, if it stops. — “Actually, the mother feels happy when the child is kicking.”

🎙 Maharaj at 34:09 (auto-transcript): “the brahma said i am you are my mother in your belly i'm kicking touching you because the mother get angry you get up to my woman don't disturb me why are you kicking me i'm cutting you don't you appreciate my sacrifice i'm cutting you for nine more don't you see i'm having…”

The child is shut in a tight place with no door, no window, no air, bent double. That has been our situation again and again.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:23 (auto-transcript): “So the woman said, yes, that is the relationship between me and you. you you are my mother and i am in the room helplessly trying to get out because i'm tight opening tight of very very tight locked up closed can you imagine no ventilation no ventilation in the in the room no…”

Even after birth we are still suffocated — not by our surroundings but by the reactions of our own sinful acts. In the womb at least we feel it.

🎙 Maharaj at 36:11 (auto-transcript): “comfortable situation no that has been our situation since all over even when we get out we are still suffocated what is suffocating us is not even the environment where we are What is suffocating us is the reaction of our sinful activities. The Bhagavatam describes the deep, pitiful prayers every one of us made in the womb — let me out and I will worship you — not once but many times. Now we have forgotten.

Helpless in the womb, we were sustained by Krishna. Now that we are out, we act independent and forget the one who helped us when we could not move.

children.note:

So Brahma asks Krishna not to take his offence seriously but to help him mature so he will not offend again. — “Brahma is very wise.”

children.topic: Inside and outside, like the airs
children.note:
Our body has airs and fires both inside and outside — fire digests food within — and a yogi can kindle fire by joining the air within to the air without. In the same way nothing is outside the Lord's energy. — “So all the elements are outside and inside.”

nodeData.topic: Day 10 · Born from You, Your Own Child
nodeData.note: SB 10.14.13-14 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Brahma pleads that he was born directly from the Lord's navel and so deserves a child's forgiveness; Maharaj shows how a king's own son, or a crying baby on a flight, is treated differently — while warning that real parents still correct. Brahma then calls Krishna the original Narayana, and Maharaj explains why the cowherd boy with two hands is the complete Supreme Person, fuller than four-armed Narayana. In the questions he insists that no one is innocent before karma, and that Brahma's bewilderment should make us more careful. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.topic: 10.14.13 — Am I not born from you?
children.note: Brahma recalls that at the dissolution Narayana lies on the waters and Brahma appears on the lotus from his navel — so is he not Krishna's own offspring? Maharaj: Brahma is right.

All living beings, moving and non-moving, come from the Lord as their father. Yesterday Krishna said Brahma was outside the womb; today Brahma adds that he came from it.

🎙 Maharaj at 42:30 (auto-transcript): “It's true. All of us, all living entities, all living entities, both moving, came about the Kassari Vishnu because he is the father,”

Brahma asks special forgiveness as the Lord's direct child. A citizen and the king's son may commit the same crime, but they are not dealt with alike: 'I know your father.'

🎙 Maharaj at 45:12 (auto-transcript): “special forgiveness for offenses. Yes, a citizen may be, some citizen may be arrested for doing something and the child of the king may do the same thing but they don't have the same permission the child of the king has a different punishment because biologically he came out from”

Brahma himself once wanted to punish a son who misbehaved before him, then forgave him because he was his child. Now he asks Krishna for the same.

🎙 Maharaj at 46:12 (auto-transcript): “forgive my foolishness forgive my misunderstanding consider me as a child after the brahma himself did that when one of his son the moon misbehaved before him but i wanted to kill him you are my son well trained a moon you don't know the etiquette grandma wait after him and…”

children.topic: The prince who was sent away
children.note:
In one kingdom the king's son kept robbing and was released every time out of respect for his father. Finally the king himself sent him out. An ideal parent does not pamper a child into ruin. — “We should not pamper the children to the point that they get spoiled.”

🎙 Maharaj at 48:42 (auto-transcript): “or the father is a king in a in a kardashim muhammad one of the kings is one of one of the kings his son was a rogue who were robbing people and he was arrested many times but when they oh it's our king's son he listened but other children were punished for the king…”

children.topic: The baby who cried all flight
children.note:
On a long flight to New Delhi a baby cried without stopping. A passenger shouted at the parents, but they never thought of throwing the child away — it was their own child, so they kept caring for it.

🎙 Maharaj at 52:06 (auto-transcript): “Therefore, I remember one time from New York City and from France to New Delhi, One child cried for friends to leave them continuously, non-stop, continuously. A parent, they tried to control the child to stop crying for the child to continue.”

Maharaj recalls how much he troubled his own mother, who carried him through rain and sun and never abandoned him. Brahma's plea is the same: consider me, I was born from you. — “I disturbed my mother day and night.”

🎙 Maharaj at 55:16 (auto-transcript): “I remember also I disturbed my mother seriously. I disturbed my mother day and night. My mother was carrying me that night alone in the rain, in the sun. She suffered. She didn't throw me away because it's a child for my womb. It's a pleasure. So the Brahma says, please…”

The Narayana here is Garbhodakasayi Vishnu, who at the dissolution takes the conditioned souls into himself and lies on the water. Brahma's special claim is that he came directly from his navel.

🎙 Maharaj at 55:59 (auto-transcript): “Narayan mentioned here is Gavodokasai Vishnu. Karavodokasai Vishnu, he has all the ingredients, all the plenitude systems of the ingredients he got from Karavodokasai Vishnu. He said, at the time of dissolution, there were entities who were pure.”

Others may or may not have come from you, Brahma says, but I certainly did. Because the Lord is our father, we too have the right to beg his causeless mercy. — “I have a special relationship with you.”

🎙 Maharaj at 58:28 (auto-transcript): “Others may or may not come from you, but certainly I am. I have a special relationship with you. in that way i'm begging for to beg for costlessness that is our our right our right because the question is our father we have a right to beg for so we'll go to text four”
Brahma declares Krishna the original Narayana, the Supersoul and witness of all, and Narayana his expansion. The purport places this after Brahma's defeat in stealing the boys and calves.

As the Gita says, Krishna pervades everything with one fragment of himself — the Supersoul alone maintains this universe. If a small part does all this, what to speak of Krishna himself? — “Small part of Krishna is doing that.”

🎙 Maharaj at 63:43 (auto-transcript): “Bhagavad Gita said, I pervade everything by one fragment of my energy. It comes in verse 12. That works. Super soul, it is super soul. Not Gavadokasai Vishnu, not Karadokasai Vishnu, not Vasudev, Sankarsan, Aniruddha, Padumna, not Mahashankarsan, not Balaran, not Krishna…”

Krishna objects: I'm a dark cowherd boy standing here, not lying on the water — how am I Narayana? Brahma replies that nara also means the living beings, whose shelter Krishna is. Krishna draws out his devotees, and they answer to teach us. — “Krishna is very, very smart, stimulating his devotees”

🎙 Maharaj at 65:14 (auto-transcript): “Krishna said, whether I am called Krishna because I am dark in color and live in Blandava. Vishnu is called Narayana because he lies in the water. How can I be Narayana? This argument, Brahma, they are conversing, Krishna is very, very smart, stimulating his devotees, and the…”

Some argue that four-armed Narayana must be greater than two-armed Krishna. Maharaj asks: four million in one hand, two in the other — which will you take? Others say Narayana is seen first, in every universe.

🎙 Maharaj at 67:38 (auto-transcript): “Some people say that Krishna, Krishna, that Kabbalah Goswami also described this in Chetan Satanga, some people say that because Narayan has four hair, and Krishna has how many? It's God. Narayan has four hands. Krishna has only two hands, four. Can you compare four to two?…”

Narayana is perfectly proper; he would never steal butter or cry before his mother. Only Krishna does such things.

🎙 Maharaj at 71:04 (auto-transcript): “And if you look at Krishna, will you see Narayan stealing water? Narayan will steal water? No? No? He will never, because he's a perfect scripturally person. He's a scripturally minded person christian activity does not they don't correspond to the scriptures so people think…”

Narayana has no father or mother, so no parental love, and no midnight dance in the forest. Krishna has neutral, servant, friendly, parental and conjugal rasa — nothing missing, even his crying is ecstasy. — “So he's complete. That's complete.”

🎙 Maharaj at 72:29 (auto-transcript): “Lord Narayan has father. Lord Narayan has father. Narayan has mother. No? So is Narayan not missing something? So Narayan not missing something? No father, no mother? So Narayan is not missing the motherly, fatherly affection. So Narayan is not missing that? Is he missing?…”

Scripture names four qualities found in Krishna and not in Narayana — the sweetness of his pastimes, his form, his flute and more. Narayana's Godhead comes from Krishna, through Balarama.

🎙 Maharaj at 75:41 (auto-transcript): “look at the philosophically scripturally four things are missing in narayan that are completing krishna what are the four things and don't see in narayan has got her he's got her but four things are not in naryan what are those four things one lila maduria thank you yes rupa…”

Entering a company you meet the security guard first and the director last; on a building site you see labourers, and the owner arrives only to collect the keys. Not seeing Krishna in creation does not mean he is not its source. — “The last person you see is the owner.”

When we enter a company, when we enter a company, whom do you see first in the company the entire company who do you see first who the first person will see the director the director no you don't see a director the security…”

This boy with a morsel of food in his hand killed mighty Aghasura, yet he carries no weapon. A weapon means someone needs protection, is afraid; Krishna is fully independent and fears no one.

🎙 Maharaj at 80:39 (auto-transcript): “krishna this is krishna so i am they himself is standing here with the muscle the foot in the left hand like uneducated baby he knows nothing but is that person who killed Agassura the mighty Agassura all the demons they are afraid of all the powerful things are what he's…”

children.topic: Q1 · Why do innocent babies suffer?
children.note:
If Krishna protects the child in the womb, why do some babies die there, and why do unwanted children survive only to suffer? Is it karma?

🎙 Maharaj at 97:33 (auto-transcript): “a question from yesterday's class this was from Reena Mataji from Brazil so Mataji was writing Hare Krishna dear Shla Gurudev the Nar Pranam please accept my humble body senses unto your divine lotus feet my question is even though Krishna helps the baby so much inside the…”

We all take birth according to past activities; a child may be ignorant of its present situation, but ignorance is no excuse. Nature takes its course. — “No one is innocent here.”

🎙 Maharaj at 98:42 (auto-transcript): “There is nothing like innocence. No one is innocent here. No one. We all take birth according to our previous sinful activities. Yeah, a child may be ignorant of the present situation, but Sr. Papa said that is not an excuse. Nature will take its course. So yes, it depends on…”

🎙 Maharaj at 99:22 (auto-transcript): “Yesterday, we had this great Sirius Prabhu, who mentioned a very incident, and his father told him a story about during the African slave trade. So the slave masters, so-called slave masters, so-called slave masters, they were killing some people and taking some people, they…”

Near the Lagos temple, a man told he would die in a road accident stopped travelling and sent his children on every errand. One day he stepped out of his front door and a tyre flying off a passing vehicle killed him. That is karma.

🎙 Maharaj at 103:42 (auto-transcript): “Here in Lagos, let me tell the one in Lagos. It won't happen in Ghana. I'll tell the one in Lagos. Not very far from Lagos Temple. Not very far from Lagos Temple. Not very far from Lagos Temple. It's a big motor park. It's a central place for markets. so it's always crowded…”

Those who keep breaking principles — even initiated devotees — should not blame guru, Krishna or family when the results arrive. No one forces us to take initiation; having accepted it, we must be careful not to add new sins.

🎙 Maharaj at 105:52 (auto-transcript): “I was telling one devotee this afternoon, you are committing sinful activities. So now you, you are thinking you are enjoying your life. Nobody talk to you and you listen. So I said, I'm praying for you, please continue to break all the principles, don't worry. I'm not…”

children.topic: Q2 · How do I stay safe?
children.note:
If Brahma with all his knowledge was bewildered, how can a small devotee stay safe, remember dependence on Krishna, and not be distracted in chanting?

🎙 Maharaj at 111:51 (auto-transcript): “We have another question from Mataji from today's class. And she's saying thank you so much for your valuable time, blessings, mercy and wonderful class. Before doing anything, a devotee asks whether it will benefit himself and other devotees or harm them, and does not jump in whimsically. Then don't misbehave and blame others.

maps.title: Brahma's Prayers · Day 11 · Hearing Is Believing

nodeData.topic: Day 11 · Hearing Is Believing
nodeData.note: SB 10.14.15-16 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Brahma asks the Lord to show the same mercy now that he showed when he first revealed himself, and Maharaj draws from Brahma's first experiences of ignorance and fear the lesson that austerity and obedient hearing come before seeing. Through Gajendra he shows that heartfelt prayer to Krishna alone is real fortune, and through the pot-and-house riddle that Krishna holds the universe while standing within it. In the questions he speaks on duty without love, the demigods, and what a guru's silence means. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Brahma, having repented his impudence, now gives reasons why the Lord should forgive him; the verse turns on the Lord being hidden from him and then suddenly revealed.

Maharaj admires Brahma's intelligence: when I searched for you in ignorance, you revealed yourself by causeless mercy; I am in the same foolish state now, so show me that mercy again.

children.topic: Not a licence to keep offending
children.note:
One might say Brahma is asking to go on offending and be forgiven. Maharaj says no: he has understood his position and is begging not to be held to his offences. — “I have done something and I came to understand my position”

🎙 Maharaj at 43:24 (auto-transcript): “same message you know one can say that yes drama you are talking like this doesn't mean that you continue to be offended yes we're helpless i'll show you my home so that means you continue to do nothing like this i have forgiven you should i continue like that that is not the…”

children.note:
As the first person, Brahma himself experienced the first things he would create: ignorance of who and where he was, then fear. We experience them after him.

Sitting on the lotus he asks where am I, why am I here, what should I do. He climbs down, finds only vast water, grows afraid and returns to his seat.

He heard the Lord but did not see him; only after his austerity did he see, and the Lord, pleased with its quality, congratulated him for satisfying him.

children.topic: Not my best — what Krishna likes
children.note:
Our right to act comes only from it pleasing Krishna. 'My best' may be poor in someone else's eyes; we should try to do what Krishna likes, not merely our best.

The scripture was revealed to Brahma; he studied it, realised it and passed it on, and it came down through Vyasa and Sukadeva Gosvami, each tasting it before giving it.

That morning they had also heard Gajendra's prayers (SB 8.3.1). Like Brahma, Gajendra prayed from the heart, and that moved the Lord.

children.topic: Can a house fit in a pot?
children.note:
Maharaj quizzes the class again and again: a pot fits inside a house, but can the house be inside the pot? Answers range from no to 'not sure' to yes, by the Lord's mercy.

children.topic: Inside and outside, like the airs
children.note:
As the airs work both within and outside the body, and a yogi can light fire without matches by connecting them, the supreme magician can be inside the universe while it is inside him. Like current that both heats and cools, Krishna has always done this — it is his nature.

Questions on duty without love, the demigods, and a silent guru.

children.topic: Q1 · Does duty without love work?
children.note:
Will doing one's duty without love help gradually, in a relationship or in devotional service?

nodeData.topic: Day 12 · Only Krishna Can Do This
nodeData.note: SB 10.14.17-18 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Brahma sees that the universe inside Krishna and the one outside are the same, and Maharaj explains why everyone, even demons, seeks a higher blessing, and why the holy name makes every flawed effort perfect. The material world is not imaginary — we feel heat, cold and hunger — but it is temporary, and only mercy reveals the Lord's deeper pastimes. In verse 18 Krishna becomes the calves, the boys and countless four-armed forms; in the questions Maharaj speaks on touching devotees' feet, pleasing the guru and why blessings come through practice. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Day 13 · The Supreme and Beautiful Person
nodeData.note: SB 10.14.19-20 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Krishna acts through Brahma, Vishnu and Siva while staying far in the background, and the ultimate truth is a supreme and beautiful person — even Sankaracarya sings of his flute and dress. He appears among every species to show he is equal to all, yet reciprocates with those who surrender, and like the sun he never really comes or goes. In the questions Maharaj explains spiritual numbness, how to deal well with others, whether Brahma is a jiva, and what was wrong with Ekalavya. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Brahma says those ignorant of the Lord's position see him only as part of the material world, though it is he who appears as Brahma, Vishnu and Siva.

children.note:

🎙 Maharaj at 58:21 (auto-transcript): “little bit we took back about a day ago it is equal yeah thank you lord christian is more merciful okay thank you lord christian is equal to all living entities is equal is equal to all not some people he wants to show he is for everyone okay very good it's equal because it's…”

If he is equal, why do only humans go back to Godhead? They don't all: Prabhupada said not many, even among devotees, would go; most would go to heaven.

children.topic: The dog and the temple rat
children.note:
Animals have gone back: Sivananda Sena's dog, delivered by Mahaprabhu; and a temple rat that kept eating ghee from the lamps, until one day a burning wick stuck to its back while arati was offered. Gajendra too. That is Krishna's impartial mercy.

The devotee's mood: the bamboo flute enjoys the nectar of Krishna's lips meant for us, and its family must be so fortunate. Our blunt senses must be purified by chanting and honouring prasadam before they can reach Krishna.

children.note:
Ekalavya made a murti of his guru and dedicated himself without initiation. Wasn't that faithfulness?

🎙 Maharaj at 99:00 (auto-transcript): “realm of reality all right my last question is from sati materji uh materji is asking what is incorrect about what a kalavya did by dedicating himself to a guru and making a murti of him without officially taking shelter of the Guru through initiation did he not show he is…”

nodeData.topic: Day 14 · One Krishna, Countless Pastimes
nodeData.note: SB 10.14.21 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Brahma admits no one can understand how the Lord's pastimes go on endlessly through his own energy. Maharaj contrasts a story of one husband who could not deal fairly with twenty-seven wives with Krishna in Dvaraka, doing something different in every queen's palace and attending 16,100 weddings in one day; Varaha shows the Lord is never degraded by the forms he takes. The recording is very fragmentary, and the reflection asks us to stop comparing our journey with others', since Krishna's care for each devotee is personal. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Brahma says no one in the three worlds can understand how and where the Lord expands his mystic energy and performs his pastimes.

Maharaj reads the verse slowly, dwelling on Brahma's admission that the Lord's spiritual potency is beyond anyone's grasp.

🎙 Maharaj at 44:10 (auto-transcript): “Also, the Dhammas, dear Godhead, no one can understand the mystery of how you are spiritual in it.”

These pastimes are going on continuously; there is no moment when Krishna is not performing them — they are happening right now.

🎙 Maharaj at 47:46 (auto-transcript): “Where past signs are taking place continuously in these three worlds. Continuously. There is no person or Christian not performing. It does not exist. This activity is right now. As Christian feels one person, it's all different.”

To show what Krishna does is impossible for anyone else, Maharaj tells of one who married twenty-seven sisters.

🎙 Maharaj at 49:44 (auto-transcript): “Julia, so far, so far. He married 27, 27 daughters. What did he do? He expanded 27 years. So how did he deal with the 27, 26, 27? He couldn't form.”

He could not manage them; he was attached to one, and the others complained they hardly felt married.

🎙 Maharaj at 50:18 (auto-transcript): “So how did he deal with the 27, 26, 27? He couldn't form. He was attached to, what was 26, are we really married? Our husband does not. See, we can't say that we are married to only one sister.”

What a human cannot do, he assumes no one can do — and so he could not function. — “What is not possible for me is also not possible for other people”

🎙 Maharaj at 51:52 (auto-transcript): “What is not possible for me is also not possible for other people, as a human being, anything like that. So now it's an anxiety. He couldn't function. I said, stay here with me. So when God was saying, we're not shaming.”

Their father warned him to care for all his daughters or be cursed, and when nothing changed the curse fell and he was afflicted.

🎙 Maharaj at 51:20 (auto-transcript): “I shall not take care of my daughters. Better take you, otherwise I will curse you. But what would he do? By the way, when he was married, he was 27 plus 31 man. What would he say married? What is not possible for me is also not possible for other people, as a human being,…”

The father demanded that Lord Siva hand him back. Siva refused: one who has taken shelter cannot be given up. So he remained only half afflicted. — “Can I give up the shelter to someone who has taken my shelter?”

Hearing that Krishna had married 16,108 wives, Narada came to see how one person could manage them.

The Dvaraka we visit today is not what it was; then it was like a universe of its own.

🎙 Maharaj at 55:22 (auto-transcript): “That time is not what we see now. Dorka is like your own universe. You have to protect us. When you see Dorka, now you think, ah, this is Dorka. No, that thing, it was different. My dear, I have a fortune. They were in my family. They had to say, all of them did together.”

In each palace Narada entered, Krishna was doing something different — one person, different activities at the same time.

🎙 Maharaj at 56:24 (auto-transcript): “When they got there, Christians were doing a different thing. They wanted to play, Christians were doing different things. children.note:
Krishna is not a demigod, not a human being, not even of the mode of goodness — he is supreme. No conditioned soul can understand his activities. — “He is supreme.”

A facilitator reads the commentary: Yogamaya presents the right pastime to each devotee at the right time. The prompt: do I feel overlooked or behind others, and what changes when I remember Krishna's relationship with me is personal and intentional?

children.note:

maps.title: Brahma's Prayers · Day 15 · A Dream Full of Miseries

nodeData.topic: Day 15 · A Dream Full of Miseries
nodeData.note: SB 10.14.22-23 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. The material world seems real, like a dream, yet brings repeated miseries; since Krishna made it, we should take his word for it, as we would a manufacturer's manual, and follow the mahajanas. It is not imaginary — we eat and feel it — but it is temporary, a school of love where we learn to serve under expert guidance. In verse 23 Krishna's body is shown to be free of material change, and Maharaj urges devotees to know their Krishna as closely as one knows someone one loves. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Brahma continues describing Krishna's inconceivable potency: by his illusory energy this temporary universe appears real like a dream, covers our consciousness and brings repeated miseries.

Maharaj stresses the words 'repeated miseries': whichever way we turn in this world, there is misery.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:21 (auto-transcript): “And Christian said, this material world is full of, full of repeated miseries, full of repeated miseries, repeated miseries, as a very important translation and words. The material world is full of repeated miseries, every direction, every direction you take, misery. Maharaj…”

Krishna himself has certified this world as temporary and miserable. Aren't we foolish to think we can make it permanent?

🎙 Maharaj at 38:01 (auto-transcript): “Yes, the same thing that Gandhi is speaking to you. This material world is temporal, full of misery. The Christian certified this material world to be temporal. And this is what the creator of the universe of the Christian said, this material world is. So are we not foolish,…”

A friend gave Maharaj a travelling bag with a padlock like two he already had. Sure he knew how it worked, he skipped the manual — and locked it shut. — “The manufacturers knows what it did.”

🎙 Maharaj at 39:06 (auto-transcript): “some years ago a friend bought me a traveling bag and then inside the bag there is a padlock i had similar padlock about two or two that was the third one they looked the same So, I was thinking, ah, it's the same thing. You don't need to look at the manual. I've seen the key…”

Brahma is only the secondary creator, working with ingredients Krishna gave him; he cannot know better than Krishna. What can we do that Brahma, thousands of times ahead of us, cannot?

🎙 Maharaj at 40:15 (auto-transcript): “world is so which among us who think that we know better even the brahma who created he is called secondary creator he's called secondary creator he created after christian has created after christian has given him all the ingredients so the brahma cannot know better than…”

Prahlada Maharaja says he fears not the Lord's ghastly form but his illusory energy, which no effort of his could overcome. Who among us knows better than Prahlada? Our security is to follow the great authorities. — “simply follow the path of the Mahajans”

🎙 Maharaj at 42:52 (auto-transcript): “If Prahlad Maharaj is speaking, this is realization. So my question remains, which among us here will know better than Prahlad Maharaj will feel the beauty? Which among us? Which of course? No one thank you. Therefore, we should simply follow. simply follow the path of the…”

'I am Miss World', 'I am the most intelligent' — these are dreams. Maharaj explains what illusion means.

🎙 Maharaj at 44:58 (auto-transcript): “so all of us are dreaming i am mrs world that's a big dream of illusion it is a dream and the most intelligent person and the most beautiful person that's a dream that's a dream yes yes that is that is that is true what when a person is when a person is sleeping so what what…”

There is no tiger in your bedroom, yet the dreamer is afraid and feels it. Only one who is awake does not feel it — so a pure devotee, not sleeping like us, is not touched by our illusion.

🎙 Maharaj at 45:39 (auto-transcript): “what is what you know the meaning of illusion what is illusion what does it mean when one is sleeping the tiger which we see is real is it not the tiger susan said but we are able to feel things yes yes yes you are correct so the when we see a tiger in the dream is it is it…”

In the dream you are a king; you wake to another troubling day. Alcohol helps us forget, but soon we are back to the same pain.

🎙 Maharaj at 46:59 (auto-transcript): “with us like us yes it is real when you are a king in the in it but when you wake up are you a king when you wake up back to frustration oh i know that's i know that's troubling day today again i wish the day didn't come but the day has come yes yes the day has come and we…”

Maharaj asks how we feel when the urge for sense gratification comes: restless, angry, helpless. What we call enjoyment is only getting free from that pain; the only solution is to wake up.

🎙 Maharaj at 47:41 (auto-transcript): “alcohol we are so we are back to the same pain so we see people who are addicted people are dictated like like all of us who are chronic sense gratifiers when there is a need to gratify the sense what how do we feel how do you feel the time for gratification or one one one…”

A dog chases water in the desert, always thinking 'next I'll get it', running until it collapses. That is material existence.

🎙 Maharaj at 52:10 (auto-transcript): “at the desert mirage is real yeah real the dog who is chasing the water in the desert if you is the water day next i'll get it next i'll get so he's only verified because he's thinking what ah next i'll get it yeah just i'll get it let me get it running and running around and…”

Yet the universe is real: when we eat a mango, an apple or a peanut we feel it, though hunger and the body come and go. Pure devotees understand this and are not in illusion. — “It is real in that sense. Only it is temporal.”

🎙 Maharaj at 53:34 (auto-transcript): “has created it yes it may be out of season sometimes but it's real when i'm taking fruit you know when i'm taking mango you know you know yes when i'm taking apple mango So it is real. You cannot say that the peanut is not real.”

We have forgotten that we are eternal servants and Krishna the eternal master, so he made this world to teach us. If we have no love for each other we cannot have love for Krishna; we must perfect our life here. — “Krishna has created the school of love for us.”

🎙 Maharaj at 55:14 (auto-transcript): “We have forgotten our service to Krishna. We have forgotten serving Krishna. Because we have forgotten that we are eternal Saravants, and Krishna is eternal Master. That we have forgotten. So to help us, Krishna has created this material. Although it is temporary, but He…”

On Gadadhara Pandita's appearance day, after an abhiseka, the senior devotees all polished Gadadhara, so Maharaj was given Nitai. He worked on long after the others left; the director then showed him spots everyone had missed, and he finished them.

nodeData.topic: Day 16 · The Guru's Light Removes Fear
nodeData.note: SB 10.14.24-25 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj explains why the spiritual master is greater than the sun: he gives the eye that sees Krishna as the soul of all souls, and his sound enters the heart through the ear. With the rope-and-snake verse he shows that only waking up through hearing ends fear, while material scientists keep us in anxiety. In the questions he speaks on tasting the holy name, wanting to chant, and crying daily for help. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Lagos, day 16: Brahma continues to glorify Krishna. The verse is about those who receive clear vision from the guru, see Krishna as the soul of all souls, and so cross material existence. Maharaj reads several translations and Bhagavad-gita 4.9.

children.topic: The guru is more than the sun
children.note:
Anyone who wants to see in the dark needs light; to understand Krishna we need scripture, and to understand scripture we need the spiritual master, here compared to the sun.

Maharaj cites a sage of the eleventh canto who says the comparison falls short: the sun shows only this world, and even that imperfectly, while the devotee gives eyes that see the spiritual world.

The sun reveals things only while it is up; when it sets, darkness returns. The vision the guru gives sees beyond matter, all the time. — “not sometimes always always always”

🎙 Maharaj at 41:59 (auto-transcript): “we need to have some idea the sun revealed other this this and and it will do that only when the sun is up so when the sun is not shining the same thing back to darkness the same darkness the spiritual massage gives the eye that we see beyond we see the material we see the…”

Ordinary eyes see buildings, trees and people absorbed in sense gratification and calling it enjoyment. The guru's gift is to see Krishna as the very soul of all souls.

Sunshine cannot make us Krishna conscious or take us back to Godhead. The spiritual master gives the eye to see the Supreme Soul and the knowledge of what we are meant to do.

children.topic: What keeps us close to Krishna
children.note:

Scripture shows where we are in the universe and where we belong; if you don't know where you are, you cannot know what to do. The Upanishads speak of the Supreme Person, and the Gita names him: Krishna. — “If you don't know where you are, you cannot know what to do.”

nodeData.topic: Day 17 · Bhakti Beyond Speculation
nodeData.note: SB 10.14.26 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj takes Brahma's lesson that bhakti is superior to speculative knowledge: for the eternally free soul both bondage and liberation are ideas born of ignorance, like paper claiming to break iron. Moving into the next verse, he shows how speculators forget both Krishna and themselves, while undivided devotion gives the access they lack. In the questions he says illusion ends when we actually hear, and the speaker's duty is simply to sow the seed. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:

The verse treats both the idea of being bound and the idea of being liberated as products of ignorance, which lose their meaning once the soul is known as distinct from matter. Maharaj reads two translations.

children.note:

nodeData.topic: Day 21 · Krishna Has Given Himself Away
nodeData.note: SB 10.14.34 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Brahma begs for mercy by glorifying Krishna honestly, and wonders what reward Krishna could give the residents of Vraja, since he has already given himself to them. Maharaj describes the heart-to-heart friendship of the cowherd boys, hearts holding nothing but Krishna, and Krishna as the property of his devotees. Questions cover the guru as friend, tasting real bhakti, Putana's family, and why Hanuman is glorified while Lakshmi is not. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Lagos. After some confusion over the text number, the class takes up the next prayer, in which Brahma seeks Krishna's mercy by glorifying him.

It is natural to praise someone whose mercy we want; materially people flatter. Brahma is not flattering — he describes the real qualities that attract him and begs with humility. — “But our system will not flatter.”

🎙 Maharaj at 42:26 (auto-transcript): “This is natural. We want to get the mercy of somebody. Even materially speaking, materially speaking you have to flatter the person. But our system will not flatter. We tell exactly what the person is. This is personal. glorify the person, tell you the qualities of that…”

We name the qualities that draw us to the person and expect that, when pleased, he will grant mercy. Brahma tells exactly the good fortune of the Vrajavasis. — “We tell exactly what the person is.”

🎙 Maharaj at 42:41 (auto-transcript): “We tell exactly what the person is. This is personal. glorify the person, tell you the qualities of that person that is attracting you to the person, and what we expect when the person is pleased, they will grant it. That is natural. We don't go to beg someone, we go to beg…”
Brahma's mind is bewildered: Krishna is every blessing, and he has already given himself to the people of Vraja — even to Putana's family — so what else could he give them?

If we went to Brahma we would ask for houses and children. Brahma asks nothing like that; he is seeing Krishna's pastimes in Vrindavan.

🎙 Maharaj at 52:38 (auto-transcript): “considering what will be happening in Brahma. If you go to Brahma, what do you say? If you go to Brahma today, what do you say? Somebody, houses, kids. The Brahma is not saying that. The Brahma is not saying that. What the Brahma is saying is different. See what Brahma is…”

Maharaj tells of the Lord guarding a devotee's door and refusing to leave without that devotee's permission. Krishna is the property of his devotees — not a lie; he demonstrated it. — “Krishna is the property of his devotees”

🎙 Maharaj at 45:41 (auto-transcript): “Until now, Lord Krishna is a security guard for the body. The demon came there too. So the demon told him, go and go and take care of the demon. Your city is the truth.”

children.topic: A king who asked for friendship

children.topic: Will Krishna be left for me?
children.note:
With a smile Maharaj voices a worry: so many are going back to Godhead — by the time I get there, will Krishna still be there for me, or will the others have taken him?

If anything better existed, Krishna would have given it to Vraja; nothing does. So pure devotees ask Krishna for nothing but his service. — “Listen, nothing is better than Krishna.”

🎙 Maharaj at 63:55 (auto-transcript): “Listen, nothing is better than Krishna. When devotees worship Krishna, they don't ask Krishna for anything. They ask Krishna only for service to Krishna. Krishna has given himself to someone else — so what will you ask for? Will you still serve, or stop? — “Your choice is only Krishna.”

🎙 Maharaj at 64:17 (auto-transcript): “So what will you ask? What will you ask? Do you have any second choice? Your choice is only Krishna. Now Krishna is given to someone else. So what will you ask? children.topic: As good as Krishna, not Krishna
children.note:
Scripture says to see the guru as good as Krishna, but that does not make him Krishna; he cannot do what Krishna does. Like iron in fire, he takes on the quality, but the difference remains. — “like a fire and an iron.”

children.note:
Vrajavasis relate to Krishna as friend or lover, not as God. At what stage does our scriptural knowledge give way to pure remembrance?

nodeData.topic: Day 22 · Same Activities, Different Heart
nodeData.note: SB 10.14.36 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. On his appearance day Maharaj explains Brahma's warning that, until we become devotees, desires are thieves, home is a prison and family affection is a chain. Sense gratification quietly steals our real self-interest and our life, while the guru keeps calling us to wake up. His puzzle for the class: the Vrajavasis do the same household work we do — the difference is that theirs is intensely engaged in pleasing Krishna. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Devotees celebrate Maharaj's appearance day. He thanks everyone who helps him in Krishna consciousness and returns to Brahma, who keeps appealing for mercy and glorifying the Vrajavasis.

The verse names three things that hold true until people become Krishna's devotees: material desire acts as a thief, the home as a prison, and family affection as a chain.

Maharaj asks what a thief is: one who takes your property without your knowledge — or, these days, openly.

🎙 Maharaj at 45:00 (auto-transcript): “devotees until we become devotees our material attachment and desires remain thieves thieves we all know what teeth means teeth teeth on who took your property without your knowledge or what your knowledge is the umbrella is a same message to you we are coming we are coming…”

He asks the class what sense gratification steals. Answers come: love for Krishna, focus, mind and intelligence, determination for sadhana, enthusiasm. Maharaj sums it up as our real self-interest, which is spiritual life. — “our self-interest is stolen by sense gratification”

🎙 Maharaj at 49:13 (auto-transcript): “since gratification is a thief a thief saying gratification is stealing what is saying of question stealing what is sense gratification stealing from us it's a question our affection for krishna good love for krishna good bhakti krishna consciousness good what is sense…”

Sense gratification destroys everything imperceptibly. Each sunrise and sunset takes our lifespan, yet we don't notice — just as a parent living with a child doesn't see it grow, while a visitor does.

A pure devotee sees that we are wasting time. Like one sleeping in a burning building, we are asleep in the lap of illusion, and the guru keeps calling us to get up. — “that is the duty of a spiritual master to constantly remind us”

nodeData.topic: Day 23 · Krishna Acts Like Us, for Us
nodeData.note: SB 10.14.37 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Brahma says the Lord, though beyond the world, plays a worldly role to increase his devotees' joy. Maharaj tells how Krishna tamed King Nagnajit's seven bulls, shows why an acarya practises like a beginner, and explains with the lamp and the diamond why Krishna's pastimes shine brightest in this dark world. In the questions he explains Krishna's special care for devotees, how to hear speakers whose conduct does not match their words, and why we fail to follow the guru's instructions. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.topic: 10.14.37 — Beyond the world, yet playing in it
children.note: Brahma's prayer today is about the Lord appearing on earth and behaving as if he were part of this world, simply to give his surrendered devotees more varieties of joy. The verse is recited and two translations are read.

Since Krishna is everything, there is no difficulty in his behaving like everything. Maharaj adds that what we see, hear and do should all be Krishna. — “whatever we hear should be krishna”

🎙 Maharaj at 35:44 (auto-transcript): “you are very worldly of this world. You behave like a part of this world. After all, Krishna is everything. So what is the difficulty? children.note:

Maharaj quizzes the class about King Nagnajit, who set a test for anyone who wanted to marry into his family: control his seven bulls.

Teaching by doing is the acarya's duty. Following Rupa Gosvami, even a pure devotee keeps the sadhana of a beginner to protect newer devotees from imitation: no one copies a hundred years of steady chanting, but everyone copies the one day it stops. — “everybody will follow that one”

children.note:
Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura's comparisons — a lamp in shade, a diamond on blue glass — explain why Krishna's pastimes amaze more in this world than in Vaikuntha. Pure devotees like Arjuna never judge Krishna by worldly standards.

In ecstasy at their praise Varaha shook his body, and the water formed a lake the demigods came to for purification. Maharaj asks where it is — Melkote in South India, where Ramanujacarya spent much time — and tells the class not to forget. — “There is no fiction in our system.”

The demigods knew Varaha was the Supreme Lord come for their good. Non-devotees understand nothing and commit offences, so what is meant for their benefit becomes their ruin.

🎙 Maharaj at 63:15 (auto-transcript): “No, they understood, this is the supreme procedure of God. And he has come for our interest. They were happy, they were happy. Non-devotis don't understand anything, therefore they will make offences. What is meant for our benefit will become our source of destruction, when…”

children.topic: He comes for his devotees' joy
children.note:
Killing demons is secondary; Krishna could do that through politicians, disease, earthquakes or famine. He comes to give his audience to devotees who serve him in disturbing circumstances. — “Krishna came to expand the joy of his devotees.”

🎙 Maharaj at 64:16 (auto-transcript): “Krishna came to expand the joy of his devotees. Not killing demons in secondary. He can do that by other means. He can do that by using our politicians, sending some disease. He can easily do that. Air quirks is there. Tornado is there. Famine is there. He can do it by all…”

Maharaj recalls how the world has crucified, poisoned, stoned and blasphemed holy persons; Krishna comes to appreciate such devotees by his presence.

🎙 Maharaj at 64:57 (auto-transcript): “or it's for the two daughters who came to this much say well that all was given anxiety by the people he tried to save so much anxieties the world is giving them anxiety this was crucified blaspheme denied Mohammed poisoned Steven stone to death many what is a necessity stone…”

His wonderful activities give devotees something to hear, discuss and meditate on, and that remembrance keeps us close to Krishna — which is his intention. — “it will keep us close with krishna”

🎙 Maharaj at 65:45 (auto-transcript): “that yes now you have something to meditate on you have something to discuss he performed these activities he devotee can talk about them devotee can hear about them devotee can meditate get absorbed in that so he did so many activities many wonderful activities marrying…”

Three questions, after a short reflection exercise led by the host.

🎙 Maharaj at 80:48 (auto-transcript): “We have our first question from Shwatana Puji. Hare Krishna Guru Maharaj, Danavad Pranam, my respectful and humble obeisances on to you. Guru Maharaj, I realized, I mean, I don't know it is my thought or, like Guru is equal to all the disciples. So Krishna is also equal to…”

children.topic: Q1 · Is Krishna equal to all?
children.note:
If Krishna, like the guru, is equal to everyone, is Radharani dearest because her service and meditation are greatest?

🎙 Maharaj at 81:05 (auto-transcript): “Hare Krishna Guru Maharaj, Danavad Pranam, my respectful and humble obeisances on to you. Guru Maharaj, I realized, I mean, I don't know it is my thought or, like Guru is equal to all the disciples. So Krishna is also equal to all the devotees, all the parts and parcels of…”

children.topic: Equal, yet a friend to devotees
children.note: Maharaj answers with the Gita's ninth chapter: Krishna envies no one, yet whoever serves him in devotion is in him and he is their friend. That is natural reciprocation, not discrimination.

Would anyone call it partiality if a worker who comes every day earns more than one who comes half the month? A company paying everyone the same would have workers who come only on payday. — “will you say it is partiality”

🎙 Maharaj at 86:07 (auto-transcript): “will you say it is partiality will you say would anyone say that is partiality if any any of our workers in your office a worker who is there eight to five pm and fully busy working very nicely 30 days working nicely and another worker is there he come to work 15 days a month…”

Some devotees speak deep philosophy but behave very differently. How can one overlook that and still relish their talks about Krishna?

🎙 Maharaj at 89:32 (auto-transcript): “Yes, Maharaj, my question is, most of the time, you talk more about the karata. the character of devotees how we have to live the rightful life and because whatever we do will go to the spiritual master my right we you demonstrate everything to us and even we are not close to…”

Sanatana Gosvami told Haridasa Thakura that many speak philosophy nicely without living it. A good brain from past karma can grasp and present the academic side, like a parrot repeating.

🎙 Maharaj at 91:10 (auto-transcript): “Thank you, thank you for your question. Yes, Sanatana Goswami, Sanatana Goswami glorified Namah Chaja Haridastra Kho. Sanatana Goswami said, my dear Haridastra, I have seen that many people, they speak the philosophy very nicely. Like you said, they know this philosophy, can…”

Talent used to please Krishna purifies; talent used for our own intellect or recognition does not, and such service fades when appreciation stops. Not everything done in a devotional setting is devotional service — only what is consciously offered for Krishna's pleasure. — “if we use our talent just entertain our own intellect we will never get purified”

🎙 Maharaj at 93:01 (auto-transcript): “is serving Krishna if we use our talent in serving Christmas sincerely will get purified if you use our talent in krishna consciousness only to entertain our own intellectual ability will never get purified as such do you understand the purification will not be as much it's…”

Watch a speaker before, while and after he speaks: if all three are consistent he is a pure devotee; if not, an orator. Maharaj recalls Kesava Kasmiri, the proud champion whose composition Mahaprabhu took apart — a torch held up to the sun.

🎙 Maharaj at 96:10 (auto-transcript): “like that orators his holiness but tomorrow says we should look at the person before he goes to speak we should look at the person while he's speaking i should look at the person what will do after speaking if the three faces are consistent means it's a pure devotee if they…”

children.topic: Go, but hear the verse and purport
children.note:
We belong to a community and should cooperate, so still attend. Fix the mind on the verse and Prabhupada's purport, and if you are eager Krishna will teach you something even through such a speaker; otherwise you leave frustrated.

children.topic: Q3 · Too weak to follow the guru?
children.note:
A question from the chat: I feel helpless and too weak to execute my guru's instructions. What can I do?

🎙 Maharaj at 103:05 (auto-transcript): “that is christmas mercy that is christmas mercy thank you so much i am very i am i am very weak to executing my guru's instruction how can i do i'm very disturbed because i feel helpless in my practices how can i do please help me that's a question from the chat box you…”

We cannot keep the instructions because we are not surrendered. Why accept someone as guru without giving ourselves? Maharaj compares it to marrying a person you do not like — no one forced you; if you are not ready, don't go; if you go, be ready to follow. — “we're not surrendered”

🎙 Maharaj at 103:49 (auto-transcript): “and this talks so what should I do we have we have answered the question many times that we are not surrender to the guru that is where we cannot keep the instructions as a problem we're not surrendered if you are surrendered you were to keep the instruction so that is it…”
Maharaj turns to the Gita 4.34 purport: approach the spiritual master in full surrender, serve without false prestige, and inquire submissively. Pleasing him is the secret of advancement.
